notes: I checked commit 4c5634b against each earlier finding in the code. Typecheck is clean and all 23 agents tests pass (~17 s). Fixed: venueTermsProblems now rejects any proposal below the 40-ticket sample cap whose implied draw does not fit the room, whatever the genre, and allows at most a 300 bps discount on the venue share. That is exactly the strongHistory discount, the only askBps term the browser and the keeper can disagree on. I replayed every dashboard-style booking (6 draws x all genres x 136 seed venues x two track records, 4,934 offers) through the keeper's rule and none was falsely rejected. Each FanSim tick now gets a buy limit of floor(left / (2 x dearest price + rent)), so a tick can no longer overshoot the run budget or the band's share. The venue model can no longer offer 0 tickets or a 0 price. A low minPrice cannot cut the price anyway, because the planner uses max(minPrice, target). Mostly fixed: each selling band gets an equal share (perRun / selling.size) and the start band rotates. Shares are per band profile, though, so one actor with k band wallets still gets k/(k+n) of the budget. The share is also recomputed every tick, so a band that starts selling after another has spent its full share early in the run gets nothing until the next run. New: under a tight share, FanSim fills a band's shows in getProgramAccounts order, so its later tour dates can starve and cancel because of the budget, not demand. The model's minPriceLamports has no upper bound in validate, and the planner books max(minPrice, target), so in auto-pilot a model answer can set the ticket price. The 'fan budget reached' log fires once per run even when only one band's share ran out, and it still reaches only the console. Still open: no test covers the per-band share, the tick limit, the in-genre fit rejection or the new venue validate (the only budget test sets the budget to 0). Cancelled and expired shows are re-read every tick. FanSim is rebuilt per run with an empty `bought`, and 'already in use' is retried. The fans' fairness re-check passes [] for other dates. The mainnet guard is a deny-list. keeper.yml still greps away the keeper's own 429 tick-failure lines. DEMO_DAY_SEC is still defined in three places. The core agent work stays strong: venue and band negotiation with track-record-aware asks, the geographic planner with travel and rest days and availability, every Claude decision validated with a heuristic fallback, and no model near a signer. The keeper is now fair per band and bounded per tick, but it is under-tested and still has rough operational edges.
